correctness.rationale: Independent construction of A5 as the 60 even permutations reproduces the class sizes 15, 20 and 24 at orders two, three and five. Exhaustive closure of all pairs and triples gives 1140 generating pairs and exactly 1240 minimal generating three-subsets. Building adjacency from those triples yields 35 nonisolated vertices, 405 edges, the degree multiset 26 repeated 15 times and 21 repeated 20 times, and exact diameter two. The structural proof also explains the census: an order-five subgroup lies in its unique maximal dihedral normalizer, while the remaining proper pair-generated subgroup types yield the stated involution and fixed-point criteria.

value.rationale: This is the smallest nonsoluble test case for the fixed-size connectivity theory and gives the complete graph structure rather than only a yes/no connectivity answer. The pair criteria, degrees and diameter make it a reusable benchmark for larger nonsoluble groups.

final_claim: The size-three independence graph of A5 has exactly 35 nonisolated vertices: all 15 involutions and all 20 elements of order three. It has 405 edges and diameter two, with involution degree 26 and three-cycle degree 21; the involutions form a clique and the three-cycle subgraph is the twofold independent blow-up of the triangular graph T(5).
limitations: Specific to A5 and the size-three layer; no all-nonsoluble-group theorem is claimed.
